evidence: Cic. Har. Resp. 2: tēla … hebetiōra (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Blunt, as against acūtus; also, of the mind or senses, dull, slow (Gell. 4.19.1).

terms.gloss: to be blunt; to be dull, sluggish

phrases.latin: Pōnite jam gladiōs hebetēs: pugnētur acūtīs.
phrases.english: Put away the blunt swords now: let the fight be with sharp ones.

phrases.latin: Quaesō, ut apparēs mihi pennam hanc. — Deest mihi gladiolus scrīptōrius. — Ēn tibi. — Hui, quam obtūsus!
phrases.english: Please trim this pen for me. — I haven’t got a penknife. — Here you are. — Goodness, how blunt it is!
phrases.source: Erasm. Coll., Euntēs in lūdum litterārium
